lines.en: : Get your fucking hands off of me you infertile, small-dicked piece of shit!
: Think you’re fucking tough because you can hold back a teenage girl?! Take me on by yourself and see how it goes, asshole! I will fucking end you!
: For the love of God, stop yelling. How many times do we have to tell you you’re not allowed here?
: I don’t answer to you, dickbag! Let me talk to whoever is in charge!
: Yeah, that’s...not gonna happen.
: Oh, and look at you! Imagine being so fucking worthless that you’re the number two to a nobody like the other fucking idiot holding me back! Suck my dick, you little bitch!
: Don’t listen to her, Gary. You’re a great guy and she doesn’t know what she’s talking about.
: Fuck you, Gary! Fuck you to Hell!
: Wha-?! What the fuck is going on over here?!
: Yumi! Thank God! Get these fucking goons off of me!
: Chika?! What the fuck are you doing here?!
: Oh, you know! Just being held back by two limp-dicked Yakuza who think they’re hot shit because they can restrain one whole girl if they work together!
: Okay. In our defense, you are freakishly strong.
: Fuck you, Gary! Yumi, help!
: Yo! Get your hands off of her! She ain’t here to cause trouble!
: But...Ojou-sama, she burst through the gates and wouldn’t even tell us-
: I don’t give a shit what she did! I said she’s alright and that means you let her the fuck go! Got it?!
: It makes sense that this girl is a friend of the princess with how strong she is.
: Ojou-sama...has a friend?...
: She’s all grown up now...
: If I have to ask again, I’m taking both of your pinkies!
: Yes, Ojou-sama!
: Gago! Supot! Putang ina mo! Kainin mo tae ko!
: Jesus. You must be really pissed off if you’re breaking out the Tagalog.
: I only remember the bad words...
: I swear to fucking God, Yumi. If those assholes messed up my wrist and I can’t use it for...stuff anymore, I’m going to take their pinkies.
: Do you...need ice or some shit?
: Hah...no. I’ll be fine in a few minutes.
: Gary bent the fucking “T” on my bracelet, though.
: Just wear the gold one instead. You have two, don’t you?
: Gold?! With this outfit?! Are you fucking kidding me?!
: Also, where the fuck have you been?!
: Uhh...h...here?
: Why?!
: Because, uhh...ain’t you, like...mad at me and shit?
: Why would that even matter?! You always said you’d rather rot in the street than come back here!
: If I knew you were back at your dad’s the whole fucking time, I wouldn’t have had to run all over the place looking for you!
: You...kinda didn’t have to, you know.
: What the fuck do you mean “I didn’t have to?”
: Well...you saw what went down. And then you said that shit about Chinami and...
: I just...figured that meant you didn’t want me around anymore...and shit.
: So what? You thought I was just never going to see you again because you beat the crap out of one girl?
: After all the shit I’ve done for you...and all the times I’ve stood up for you...you think one thing will just make me go, “Welp. Yumi sucks. Guess my best friend is Chinami now?”
: I got no fuckin’ clue, Chika. All that shit happened so fuckin’ fast that I didn’t know what to do or where to go.
: I didn’t want to come back here. Made me feel like a fuckin’ failure.
: Livin’ on the streets is...sketchy, though. Gives me the fuckin’ creeps. Couldn’t even get to sleep cause I always felt like somebody was watchin’ me.
: All you had to do was talk to me.
: Yeah, well...you know I ain’t that good at that either.
: Least nobody asks me shit here. And I’ve got a bed and...all the food I can fuckin’ eat too.
: So...I came all the way here for nothing and you’re just going to ghost on me now?
: It ain’t like that.
: Then tell me what it’s like, Yumi. Because I’ve seen you do a ton of crazy shit before, but never anything like that. That was a new level of anger that I...I wasn’t ready for yet.
: And yet you were about to kill two Yamaguchi officers just now.
: Yeah, well they picked a fight with the wrong bitch and I will fucking cut anyone who stands between me and what I love.
: That’s what I’ve always liked about you.
: Is it? You didn’t just stick around for fashion tips?
: Speaking of which, your boobs look great in that top. You’re not still wrapping them, are you?
: Is that...really what we’re gonna talk about?
: Well, are you actually going to talk about what I came here to talk about? Or are you going to be a fucking lonely cunt like always and try to figure this out on your own as well?

: I don’t fuckin’ know, Chika. But can we at least sit down if we’re gonna talk about this shit? Barely slept at all last night and my legs are fuckin’ killing me from doin’ so many laps around this place.
: Depends on if your goons are going to assault me again for setting foot on their beloved walkway.
: They’ll do whatever the fuck I tell ‘em to. I’m still the boss’s daughter even if I ain’t been here in a hot minute.
: Okay. But if I so much as see Gary again, I swear to fucking God.
: Gary really ain’t that bad. He’s one of the good ones.
: Gary can go to Hell.
Through openings in the wood, the sun beats down on the backs of two girls who may appear to be close at the moment, but could not be any further away when you really start to think about it.
This is speaking figuratively, of course. But given the amount of exposure you’ve had to these long-winded ramblings of mine, I’m sure I don’t have to tell you that.
The one on the right wants to know everything.
She wants to know why a girl she believed was getting better relapsed.
She can’t help but draw parallels to her best friend’s mother and how things like that might just run in the family.
But those are thoughts she hates herself for having.
The one on the left just wants it all to stop.
She doesn’t want to talk about this. But, at the same time, she doesn’t regret anything at all.
She, too, draws parallels to her mother. It’s all too easy when the lines outstretch toward her and her alone.
She thinks that maybe this is all she’s good for...and that the idea of ever trying to fit in or survive outside of these walls in the first place was nothing short of a pipe dream.
But more than that, she’s worried the truth will get out.
She’s worried that it won’t just stop at what happened in the locker room-
But that revealing the true nature of that unfortunate night will open the flood gates and she won’t be able to hold back everything else that’s happened.
She won’t be able to hold back how unclean it all feels.
Or how she’s still too curious to just rinse it all off.
But more than that...she’s worried about hurting her one and only friend-
And that confessing to what happened in the locker room on that unfortunate night will snowball into something that could result in more than just the shattering of herself.
The girl on the left knows for certain of the futility of the love her best friend pursues.
But her desire to see an honest smile on a bronze tinted face outweighs her desire to rid herself of the scattered impurities brought to light by someone who had it out for her.
And deep down, she can’t help but feel as if she deserved it.
: Have you talked to your dad at all?
: For a minute or two. But it was the same old shit it’s always been. Dude’s still an asshole. But he’s an asshole with a house and I kinda figured I didn’t have a place to go anymore.
: Ain’t even allowed to come get my shit at the dorms since it’s technically school property. But I guess it ain’t like I’ve got much there to begin with.
: Anybody else here able to...you know...help get your mind off of stuff? Any of those guys you used to hang around with?
: Nah. Heard a few of ‘em died from some of the older guys who are still here, though. Sucks.
: So you’ve just been...wandering around all sad and lonely this whole time?
: It ain’t been that bad. At the very least, I can be alone here. And nobody’s ever gonna start shit with me.
: Still would’ve been nice to have you here, though. One of the very few people that hasn’t really pissed me off yet.
: Okay, now you’re straight up lying because I know for a fact that I piss you off every single morning.
: Yeah, but there’s a big difference between pissing me off because you take six hours to get ready and, like...actually pissing me off.
: Beauty doesn’t come without its setbacks, Yumi. Just because it takes you five minutes to get ready doesn’t mean we can all be that lucky.
: Heh...me...lucky. That’s rich.
: Are you gonna tell me what happened?
: You saw what happened.
: Ooookay. Then, are you going to tell me why it happened?
: Yumi, do you really think I would have trespassed on Yakuza turf and fought off two thugs if I didn’t want to be on your side? Fuck no.
: I’m basically dying for a reason to go to bat for you right now. But shit like “Oh, you guys just don’t understand her!” isn’t going to work this time.
: Nodoka was fucked up for like a whole week. I’m surprised she came out of that without a concussion.
: How about everybody else?
: What do you mean?
: What are they sayin’ about me?
: If you need to “go to bat” for me...it’s probably pretty bad, huh?
: It’s...uhh...
: It’s definitely...not good...
: Your reputation kinda sucked to begin with and beating a genius unconscious while she was trying to teach the nicest girl in the class math is...not a good look.
: Figured.
: But, Yumi! You-
: Maybe I just felt like beatin’ the shit out of her, Chika?
: But, that...
: No way. That wouldn’t make any sense.
: Why not? Bullied Futaba from the moment I met her. Tons of other people too.
: Still talk mad shit on Sensei and you guys are basically attached at the hip now.
: Maybe I just ain’t a good person?
: Yeah...maybe you’re not. But you’re also not the type of person to just do shit like that without a reason.
: You also thought I wasn’t the type of person to come back here of all places and I didn’t even last one day out on the streets.
: Yumi-
: People change, Chika. You gotta remember where I come from.
: I’m the daughter of a Yakuza boss and a junkie. Ain’t exactly the model family a lot of other people grow up with.
: Why are you hiding this from me?
: Who says I’m hiding anything?
: You think I don’t understand your stupid mannerisms by now? How you always look away and drop your voice whenever you’re trying to keep something a secret?
: Did I fuck up guessing where you went? Yeah. Yeah, I did. But I was also holding out hope that you were going to come back to my family before the one you left to try and become a better you.
: Chinami is worried sick. We want you back.
: But right now, what I want more than anything is to understand what happened to you so you don’t just...lose all of the progress you’ve made.
: Honestly, Chika...fuck progress. The hell was I going to get out of that anyway?
: Ain’t like I was tryin’ to make friends or something. If anything, I don’t even know if I’d call any of that “progress” since I was just...backtracking on all of the bad shit I’ve done.

: No reason to clap and cheer for me for finally turning around when I’ve been runnin’ the race in the wrong direction my whole life. Might as well just...quit and save myself the embarrassment, you know?
: I don’t...but I’m going to clap and cheer for you any chance I get since you’re my best friend. I just wish you’d trust me enough to confide in me.
: Course I trust you. Maybe I just don’t want you catchin’ a murder charge and leaving the twerp all on her own when she’s already lost everybody else?
: A...murder charge? Just what the fuck happened?
: Doesn’t matter. It’s in the past now.
: So my reputation is dead in the water. Big deal. Ain’t like I’m ever comin’ back to school in the first place.
: What do you mean “ever?”
: Were you actually expelled? Because word around the school is that you’re just indefinitely suspended. Which means that there’s still hope for-
: Think I’m just gonna drop out.
: What?...
: Let’s be real. I never fit in there anyway. And if we had any other teacher, I probably would’ve been kicked out already.

: But...no. No, I can’t let you do that. You always talk about how you want to make something of yourself and...and if you’re dropping out...what are you going to do instead? What does that mean for us?
: For us? Not much. If you ain’t scared of me after almost killin’ Nodoka and shit, I’m happy to keep bein’ friends with you.
: But for me?
: I don’t know.
: Maybe I’ll hang out here for a while? Give the whole Yakuza princess shit a spin and see how that goes.
: That’s...
: But that’s...the exact opposite of what you’ve been trying to do this whole time.
: It is, ain’t it?
: Means it might actually work.
: Besides, as long as I don’t end up like my mom, I think I’ll be able to call my life a success. And I ain’t anywhere near that bad yet.
: Hey now. I’ve been gettin’ a hell of a lot better, you know.
